citation: J. E. Thornton, "Design of a Computer: The Control Data 6600", Scott, Foresman and Co., 1970
title: Design of a Computer: The Control Data 6600

segments.title: Front matter
segments.why: The front matter lists instructions and execution times but provides no arithmetic-unit design detail.

segments.title: INTRODUCTION
segments.why: The introduction discusses motivation and functional parallelism without describing arithmetic mechanisms.

segments.title: ORGANIZATION OF THE 6600
segments.why: The chapter presents system organization and peripheral/processor separation rather than arithmetic-unit mechanisms.

segments.title: BASIC CIRCUIT PROPERTIES
segments.why: The chapter covers transistors, circuits, packaging, power, and wiring as general implementation technology.

segments.title: CENTRAL STORAGE SYSTEM
segments.why: The chapter describes magnetic-core storage organization and memory access mechanisms.

segments.title: CENTRAL PROCESSOR FUNCTIONAL UNITS
segments.why: The chapter gives design detail for the fixed/increment/floating adders, carry-save multiplier, iterative divider, shift network, and population-count hardware.

segments.title: CENTRAL PROCESSOR CONTROL
segments.why: The chapter concerns instruction issue, scoreboarding, interrupts, and register control rather than arithmetic-unit implementation.

segments.title: PERIPHERAL SUBSYSTEM
segments.why: The chapter describes peripheral processors, channels, devices, and input/output control.

segments.title: SYSTEMS OPERATION
segments.why: The chapter covers operating-system files, tables, job scheduling, and resource management.

segments.title: APPENDIX
segments.why: The appendix provides instruction timing and issue constraints as back matter without defining arithmetic mechanisms.

segments.title: INDEX
segments.why: The index is back matter rather than a chapter containing design exposition.
